[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc3Foundations Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The foundations module contains features related to founding and core beliefs/principles of the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1a", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u26ea Churches", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Churches list holds your church. Once Enable Multi-Church is switched on in Church Features, it can also hold branch or satellite churches: mark the main church Is Group, then add each branch with the main church as its Parent Church. There is always exactly one main church (the one without a parent).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1website01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What each church shows on the public website. Tick Publish to put the church on the site, then fill in:
- About and Mission Statement, which its About Us page uses
- Image, a photo or logo for its card on the Locations page
- Address, Phone and Email, which the footer and the Contact Us page use
Leave Phone or Email blank and the church shows whatever is in Contact Us Settings, which is shared by the whole site. The Website manual covers how visitors move between locations.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1print001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "These details also print. Anything you print for a branch church, such as a giving statement, carries that church's own name and contact line rather than the main church's. Legal Name and Tax ID work differently: leave them blank on a branch and it prints the main church's, because the main church is usually the registered charity that issues the receipt.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In multi-church mode every church-specific record (Person, Family, Prayer Request, Function, Fund, Collection, Bulletin and so on) gains a Church field, shown near the top of the form and as a standard list filter. New records default to the church of the person saving them. Records that belong to another record (a sign-up to its function, a care request to its person) take that record's church automatically, and a family belongs to the church of its head of household. The Church Directory still lists a family under every branch that has one of its members. Single-church sites never see the field.

Some records can be handed to every church instead of being kept by one. These carry a Shared with all churches tick box: songs, sermons, sermon series and handouts, vendors, rooms, locations and assets, the occasions churches hold together, which are functions and meeting minutes, and the two things money runs through, funds and ministries. Sharing is one record at a time, never a whole type: nothing is shared until somebody ticks the box on that record. Tick it and every church can see and use it, whichever church shared it, and the Church field disappears because the record no longer belongs to one.

Shared By on the record names the church that shared it, and you can filter a list by it to separate what you shared from what was shared with you. Open a record another church shared and a note at the top says so, with the tick box locked.

Only the church that shared a record can stop sharing it, or delete it. Untick the box there and the record goes back to that church and leaves everyone else's lists, and anything attached to it, such as a booking of a shared room, goes back with it. A branch that no longer wants something shared with it has to ask the church that shared it, so one branch cannot take a resource away from the rest. Anything attached to a shared record is shared along with it, such as a booking of a shared room or a sign-up to a shared function, so every church sees the same diary and the same list of names. Gifts and expenses are never shared: each one keeps the church that gave or spent it, so every report shows a church only its own money. A shared fund or ministry therefore shows its joint figures to every church that can see it: the fund's balance and list of transactions, the ministry's running total of what has been spent on it. People and attendance are never shared.

A Budget tracks the spending of its own church. Tick Include Branch Churches on it to count what the churches beneath it spend as well, which is how the main church budgets for everyone at once.

The Church record also holds the church's Mission Statement and a Church Verse (a Bible Reference). It can also carry an Image, such as a logo. Bulletins print the verse on the back cover and the image on the front cover when the Church Verse and Church Image sections are switched on. A branch that leaves Legal Name, Tax ID or Default Bible Translation blank uses its parent's.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1f", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Turning Enable Multi-Church on stamps the main church on every existing record and gives every existing user a permission for the main church with branches hidden, so nothing becomes visible to anyone by accident. It cannot be turned off again while branch churches exist.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1d", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who Sees Which Church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Everyone sees the records of their own church, and nothing from the others. Someone at a branch sees that branch's events, prayer requests and giving. The main church's records stay out of their way, and theirs stay out of the main church's.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1dir1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "One people directory", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1dir2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People and families are the exception. Every church can look up every Person and Family, so a branch can find a visitor from the main church, choose a main-church pastor as a counselor or speaker, or check in a family from another campus. The Church field on each person shows which church they belong to.
- Only a person's own church can change them. Another church sees the form as read-only.
- To move someone to another church, use a Member Transfer.
- Prayer requests, care, counseling, visitation and giving stay with each church, whichever directory setting you use.

To hide each church's people and families from the other churches, tick Keep People and Families Private to Each Church in Church Features. The Check-In Station still finds everyone at a function that is shared with all churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Where a person's church comes from", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "From the Church field on their Person record. Fill that in, link them to a login (the Invite to Portal button does this for you), and they can see that church and no other. There is nothing else to set up.
If they later move to another church, change the same field, or confirm a Member Transfer with a To Church. What they can see moves with them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People who belong to one church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Most people. They never have to choose a church, so the app stops asking: the Church field is hidden on their forms, the Church filter is hidden on their lists and reports, and anything they create belongs to their church automatically.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Seeing the branches as well", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Someone at a church that has branches beneath it still sees only their own church to begin with. To bring the branches in, choose Include Branch Churches from the menu at the top left. While the branches are included:
- a blue note sits at the top of every page, so nobody forgets they are looking at more than their own church
- that same menu item now reads Hide Branch Churches, which puts things back
- lists and reports gain a Church box. Leave it empty to see every church at once, or pick one church to see only that church.
- ticking Expand filters to branches on the blue note changes that last point: picking a church then shows its branches too. This is remembered for that person alone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People who see everything", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two kinds of account: the built-in Administrator, which the app never restricts, and anyone who has not been given a church. Their reports still open on the main church, so clear the Church box to see every church at once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e10", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If someone sees the wrong thing", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e11", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Check the Church field on their Person record first, since that is what drives everything else. What it creates behind the scenes is a User Permission, which an administrator can look at or change there directly. A change made by hand stays until that person's church or login changes, at which point it is set again from their Person record.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fQeaH6cwov", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Note: Without multi-church, only one Church record is allowed. With it, only one main church (a church without a Parent Church) is allowed; every other church must have a Parent Church that is marked Is Group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w8oEjl0tNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcd4Beliefs", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rx8sNKF0oc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Beliefs are the foundational principles the church stands for.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nVhOr1yDL4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding church beliefs, note the following:
- Type the Bible references each belief rests on, such as Romans 3:23; Ephesians 2:8-9. They show beneath the statement on the Beliefs web page.", "col": 12}}]
